name: pyannote/speaker-diarization
pricingModel: Free self-hosted (Estimated GPU infra: $0.06/hr on A10G)
description: Pretrained neural speaker diarization pipeline based on pyannote.audio. Features end-to-end speaker segmentation, overlap-aware embeddings, and agglomerative hierarchical clustering.
strengths: Gold-standard open research baseline
Robust overlapping speech detection
Full offline execution with strict zero-data-retention compliance
limitations: Offline batch only (no native chunk-based streaming pipeline)
High GPU VRAM requirement for long multi-hour files without VAD chunking

name: NeMo Sortformer / MSDD
pricingModel: Free self-hosted (Estimated GPU infra: $0.08/hr on A100/L4)
description: NVIDIA NeMo diarization stack utilizing Multi-Scale Diarization Decoder (MSDD) and Sortformer multi-speaker transformer architectures. Optimized with TensorRT for high throughput.
strengths: Highly optimized GPU throughput with TensorRT inference engines
Strong cluster separation in structured meeting corpora
limitations: Complex dependency chain and container setup
Sensitivity to telephone band-pass artifacts without domain adaptation

name: DiariZen
pricingModel: Free self-hosted (Estimated GPU infra: $0.05/hr on T4/A10G)
description: State-of-the-art diarization recipes from Brno University of Technology (BUT), consistent winners of DIHARD and CHiME evaluations. Leverages Bayesian HMM x-vector clustering and neural speech activity detectors.
strengths: DIHARD-grade accuracy on challenging noisy, unconstrained domains
Very low false alarm rate on quiet transitions and room acoustics
limitations: Academic recipe codebase with steeper integration curve than pip packages
Multi-stage pipeline requiring careful intermediate feature caching

name: pyannoteAI Precision
description: Production-grade managed SaaS offering by the original authors of pyannote.audio. Enhanced proprietary neural models trained on massive private voice corpora with accelerated inference.
strengths: Exceptional accuracy on overlapping speech segments
Direct RTTM and structured JSON timestamps with speaker turn continuity
No speech recognition overhead when only diarization labels are needed
limitations: Pure diarization service: does not produce text transcripts natively
Streaming track currently not public on general tier

name: Deepgram Nova
description: End-to-end deep learning speech platform providing simultaneous automatic speech recognition and diarization with ultra-fast RTF (<0.05) and low-latency WebSocket live streaming.
strengths: Industry-leading inference speed and streaming real-time factor
Cost-effective combined STT + diarization pricing
Native WebSocket streaming support for live voice agents
limitations: Higher speaker confusion when rapid backchannels overlap primary speaker
Boundary collar precision slightly wider on brief interjections

name: AssemblyAI Universal
description: Speech-to-text API featuring 'Speaker Diarization v3' with enhanced clustering, punctuation-aligned word boundaries, and automatic speaker count estimation.
strengths: Tightly aligned word-level timestamps and punctuation
Accurate speaker count on 2-4 speaker podcast and interview settings
Comprehensive developer SDKs and webhook tooling
limitations: Diarization is tightly coupled to STT word emission boundaries
Streaming diarization has restricted capability compared to batch

name: Speechmatics Ursa
description: Autonomous Speech Recognition engine specialized in global accents, dialect tolerance, and high-accuracy multi-speaker conversational flow in both batch and live WebSocket streaming.
strengths: Remarkable resilience to Indian English, regional accents, and Hinglish code-switching
Very low speaker confusion in phone-line 8kHz audio
Enterprise on-prem container deployment availability
limitations: Higher price point per audio hour than mass-market providers
Slightly longer initial warm-up latency on cold streaming handshakes

name: Cloud STT v2
description: Google Cloud Speech-to-Text v2 API with Chirp foundation models and speaker diarization config. Supports streaming gRPC and batch Cloud Storage processing.
strengths: Global language coverage and Chirp foundation model acoustic depth
Direct integration with GCP IAM, BigQuery, and Pub/Sub pipelines
limitations: Speaker diarization requires tuning `minSpeakerCount` and `maxSpeakerCount` hints for optimal clustering
Higher missed speech on simultaneous overlapping talkers

name: AWS Transcribe
description: Fully managed speech recognition service with Speaker Partitioning, Channel Identification, and PII redaction. Supports both asynchronous S3 batch jobs and HTTP/2 live streaming.
strengths: High compliance certifications (HIPAA eligible, FedRAMP, SOC2)
Channel diarization for dual-track call center systems
limitations: Historically higher DER on spontaneous conversational overlaps
Strict collar boundaries occasionally truncate soft word-final sounds

name: Azure AI Speech
description: Microsoft Cognitive Services Speech SDK offering conversation transcription, multi-microphone array beamforming diarization, and batch transcription with speaker diarization.
strengths: Excellent multi-channel beamforming integration when circular mic arrays are present
Native Microsoft Teams and Office ecosystem alignment
limitations: Single-channel blind speaker count often over-estimates quiet speakers
Setup requires Azure tenant and complex SDK initialization

name: ElevenLabs Scribe
description: Next-generation multi-speaker transcription and diarization API designed for high fidelity, character-level timestamps, and expressive voice segmentation.
strengths: Strong voice feature extraction on clean studio and podcast audio
Modern ergonomic developer REST API and SDK
limitations: Newer product entry: limited historical benchmark calibration on noisy rooms
Batch mode only currently without live agent WebSockets

name: Gladia Solaria
description: Fast multi-lingual audio intelligence engine optimized for real-time and async transcription with built-in enhanced diarization, audio intelligence, and translation.
strengths: Fast processing with low real-time factor across multi-lingual conversations
Flexible audio intelligence add-ons (summarization, chapters, sentiment)
limitations: Occasional speaker ID drift over long recordings (>60 min)
Strict collar boundary can produce false alarms on background office chatter
